page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 128 GB of RAM, providing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on remote network storage and external hardware for persistent data and GPU tasks. Baseline network performance is rated at 32 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates high multi-core scaling. Results highlight strong performance in multi-core CPU workloads, software compilation via Clang, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. Single-core tests, such as single-threaded gzip compression and standard memory bandwidth measurements, fall into average performance tiers. Additionally, execution of small LLM prompt processing and text generation scores within the top performance quarter, while medium model inference rates remain average.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration offers effective resource density for compute-bound multi-threaded applications that do not require high memory-per-core allocations. Lacking local storage, it incurs network storage dependency for IOPS-intensive applications but excels in compute efficiency for stateless parallel processing. The server is suited for software build pipelines, multi-threaded data compression, database server hosting, image processing services, and high-concurrency web applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B CPU at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 128 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation suited for thread-dense processing. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing a 32 Gbps network interface for network-attached services. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core performance in software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and image processing, while single-core metrics and memory bandwidth maintain average baseline scores. The underlying x86_64 architecture includes vector instructions such as AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions. Without bundled local disk resources, storage must be attached over the network interface. Overall, the configuration provides efficient resource density for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation workloads, concurrent web servers, and small-scale machine learning inference pipelines.
